source.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset and David Brown
source.edition: CCEL expanded electronic edition of the 1871 public-domain text

entries.heading: Verse 1
entries.text: Ps 140:1-13 . The style of this Psalm resembles those of David in the former part of the book, presenting the usual complaint, prayer, and confident hope of relief.
2-5. This character of the wicked, and the devices planned against the pious, correspond to Ps 10:7; 31:13; 58:4 , &c.

entries.heading: 3. sharpened . . . like a serpent
entries.text: 3. sharpened . . . like a serpent --not like a serpent does, but they are thus like a serpent in cunning and venom.

entries.heading: 7. day of battle
entries.text: 7. day of battle --literally, "of armor," that is, when using it.
8. (Compare Ps 37:12; 66:7 ). lest they exalt themselves --or, they will be exalted if permitted to prosper.
9. Contrasts his head covered by God ( Ps 140:7 ) with theirs, or (as "head" may be used for "persons") with them, covered with the results of their wicked deeds ( Ps 7:16 ).
10. (Compare Ps 11:6; 120:4 ). cast into the fire; into deep pits --figures for utter destruction.

entries.heading: 11. an evil speaker
entries.text: 11. an evil speaker --or, "slanderer" will not be tolerated ( Ps 101:7 ). The last clause may be translated: "an evil (man) He (God) shall hunt," &c.
13. After all changes, the righteous shall have cause for praise. Such shall dwell --shall sit securely, under God's protection ( Ps 21:6; 41:12 ).
